title: Pattern Around Us: Number and Shape Patterns
seo_title: Number and Shape Patterns Class 4 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 3)
standard_code: Class 4, Maths Mela Chapter 3: Pattern Around Us
standard_text: Patterns: identifying, extending and creating shape and number patterns, finding the rule, and odd and even numbers (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Pattern Around Us worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 3): repeating and growing patterns, rules, odd and even numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find the rule, then use it.
key_sub: Growing patterns change by the same amount each time.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Repeating patterns repeat a core: ▲●●▲●●.
  • Growing patterns change by a rule: 4, 7, 10, 13 (add 3).
  • Even + even = even, odd + odd = even, odd + even = odd.

Examples

Example

What comes next: 5, 9, 13, 17, …?

Add 4 each time

Answer: 21

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the first difference onlyCheck the rule works for every step.
Thinking odd + odd is odd3 + 5 = 8, which is even.

faq.a: The instruction that makes each term from the one before, such as 'add 5'.

faq.q: Why are odd + odd numbers even?
faq.a: The two odd ones pair up to make a pair.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is red triangle, blue circle, blue circle, yellow square. The last one shown is the 1st element of a core, so next comes blue circle. After a red triangle come two blue circles.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is up, right, down, left. The last one shown is the 3rd element of a core, so next comes left. Each arrow makes a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: What is the core of this number pattern?
items.e: The numbers go 2, 5, 5, 8, then 2 again. The core is 2, 5, 5, 8. “2, 5” is too short: after 5 comes another 5.

items.q: What is the core of this pattern?
items.e: The core is the shortest part that repeats from the start. Here it is star, star, square, circle, and then it starts again. There are two stars in each core, not one.

items.q: Which letters show the same pattern?
c: A B C A B C A B
A A B C A A B C
A B B C A B B C
A B B A B B A B
items.e: Red triangle is A, blue circle is B and yellow square is C. The core is A, B, B, C, so the pattern is A B B C A B B C.

items.q: How many elements are in the core of this pattern?
items.e: The core is star, star, square, circle. That is 4 elements. 3 counts the different shapes, but the star is in the core twice.

items.q: Which pattern has the same core structure as red, red, blue, red, red, blue?
items.e: Red, red, blue is A, A, B. The numbers 2, 2, 7 are also A, A, B. So the answer is 2, 2, 7, 2, 2, 7.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a repeating pattern?
c: A B B A B B A B B
A A B A A B A A B
A B B A B A A B
A B C D A B C D
items.e: The others repeat the same core each time. A B B A B A A B has no part that repeats the same way.

items.q: Siddharth makes a sound pattern. What are the next two sounds?
items.e: The core is clap, snap, snap, stomp. The row ends with clap, snap. Next come snap, stomp. There are two snaps in each core.

items.q: This pattern has one mistake. Which shape is wrong?
items.e: The core is red triangle, blue circle, blue circle, yellow square. Yellow squares go at 4, 8 and 12. Shape 7 should be a blue circle.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What is the 10th number?
items.e: The core is 4, 1, 6. 10 = 3 × 3 + 1, so the 10th number is the 1st number of a core: 4. 10 is the position, not the number in that position.

items.q: The pattern keeps repeating. What shape is the 12th shape?
items.e: The core has 3 elements. 12 = 3 × 4, so the 12th element is the last element of a core: square. Check: squares are at 3, 6, 9, 12.

items.q: The pattern repeats. Which way does the 15th arrow point?
items.e: The core is up, right, down, left (4 arrows). 15 = 4 × 3 + 3, so the 15th arrow is the 3rd arrow of a core: down. Check: down arrows are at 3, 7, 11, 15.

items.q: The pattern keeps repeating. What colour is the 20th circle?
items.e: The core has 3 elements. 20 = 3 × 6 + 2, so the 20th element is the 2nd element of a core: blue. Check: the blue ones are at 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20.

items.q: The pattern keeps repeating. What is the position of the next yellow square?
items.e: Yellow squares are the 4th element of each core. They are at 4, 8, 12. 8 is the last yellow square shown.

items.q: The pattern keeps repeating. What shape is the 25th shape?
items.e: The core has 3 elements. 25 = 3 × 8 + 1, so the 25th element is the 1st element of a core: triangle. Check: triangles are at 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25.
The core has 4 elements. 22 = 4 × 5 + 2, so the 22nd element is the 2nd element of a core: yellow. Check: the yellow ones are at 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22.

items.q: A pattern has the core red, blue, blue, yellow. It has 20 shapes. How many blue shapes are there?
items.e: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cores. Each core has 2 blue shapes. 5 × 2 = 10. 5 counts only 1 blue in each core.

items.q: Zoya makes a bracelet with 30 beads. The core is red, red, white. How many white beads are there?
items.e: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cores. Each core has 1 white bead, so there are 10 white beads. 20 is the number of red beads.

items.q: A pattern has the core A, B, C, D, E. What is the 23rd letter?
items.e: The core has 5 letters. 23 = 5 × 4 + 3, so the 23rd letter is the 3rd letter of a core: C. Check: C is at 3, 8, 13, 18, 23.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. Each figure has 3 more sticks. 10 + 3 = 13 sticks in Figure 4. 16 counts 4 sticks for every square, but squares next to each other share a stick.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure has 2 more chairs. 8 + 2 = 10 chairs in Figure 4. 16 counts 4 chairs for every table, but no chairs fit where tables touch.

items.q: In this table, 16 is under 5. What does that mean?
items.e: Read down the column: the figure number is on top and the number of sticks is below. So Figure 5 has 16 sticks.

items.q: This table of values shows a pattern. How many cubes are in Figure 7?
items.e: The number of cubes goes up by 3 each time. Keep going: 15, 18, 21, 24. Figure 7 has 24 cubes. 42 is 7 × 6, but only Figure 1 has 6 cubes.

items.q: What number is missing from the table of values?
items.e: The number of sticks goes up by 2 each time: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. The missing number is 9. 4 is the figure number, not the number of sticks.

items.q: What figure number is missing from the table?
items.e: The figure numbers count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The missing figure number is 3. 8 is the number of chairs in Figure 3.

items.q: This table of values shows a pattern. How many sticks are in Figure 8?
items.e: The number of sticks goes up by 3 each time. Keep going: 13, 16, 19, 22, 25. Figure 8 has 25 sticks. 28 is one jump too many. 32 is 8 × 4.

items.q: This table of values shows a pattern. How many tiles are in Figure 5?
items.e: The number of tiles goes down by 2 each time. Keep going: 6, 4. Figure 5 has 4 tiles. This pattern is shrinking.

items.q: The graph shows a growing pattern. What does the point above 3 show?
items.e: The figure number is along the bottom. The number of cubes is up the side. The point above 3 is at 12, so Figure 3 has 12 cubes.

items.q: The graph shows a growing pattern. How much does each point go up?
items.e: The points are at 5, 10, 15, 20. Each one is 5 more. 1 counts one grid line, but each grid line is worth 5. 20 is the value of Figure 4.

items.q: The graph shows the chairs in each figure of a pattern. The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 5?
items.e: Read the points: 4, 6, 8, 10. Each point is 2 higher. 10 + 2 = 12 chairs. 10 is Figure 4.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of cubes?
c: Start at 3 and add 6 each time
Start at 6 and add 6 each time
Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 6 and add 3 each time
items.e: Count: 6, 9, 12. Figure 1 has 6 cubes and each figure adds a tower of 3. The rule is start at 6 and add 3 each time. 6 is the start, not the jump.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of sticks?
c: Start at 2 and add 3 each time
Start at 3 and add 2 each time
Start at 1 and add 2 each time
Start at 3 and add 3 each time
items.e: The bottom row starts at 3. 3 + 2 = 5, 5 + 2 = 7, 7 + 2 = 9. The rule is start at 3 and add 2 each time.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 14 chairs?
items.e: Keep going: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Figure 6 has 14 chairs. 14 is the number of chairs, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 9 tiles?
items.e: The points go 1, 3, 5, 7. Each is 2 more, so the next point is 9. That is Figure 5. 9 is the number of tiles, not the figure number.

items.q: Which table of values follows the rule “Start at 6 and add 4 each time”?
items.e: Figure 1 has 6. Then add 4: 6, 10, 14, 18. The answer is 6, 10, 14, 18. 10, 14, 18, 22 adds 4 before the first figure.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 5?
items.e: Count: 1, 3, 6. The jumps are +2, then +3, so the next jumps are +4 and +5: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15. 9 uses only the first step (+2) each time.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 10?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 2 each time. From Figure 1 to Figure 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 2 = 18. 4 + 18 = 22. 40 is 10 × 4, but only Figure 1 has 4 chairs.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many dots are in Figure 12?
items.e: Each figure is a row of 5 more dots. Figure 12 has 12 rows: 12 × 5 = 60. 55 is Figure 11.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 31 sticks?
items.e: Keep going: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28, 31. Figure 10 has 31 sticks. 31 is the number of sticks, not the figure number.

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 5 and add 3 each time”?
items.e: The first number is 5. Then add 3: 5 + 3 = 8, 8 + 3 = 11, 11 + 3 = 14. The answer is 5, 8, 11, 14. 8, 11, 14, 17 adds 3 before the first number.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 5 and add 3 each time
Start at 8 and add 3 each time
Start at 5 and add 5 each time
items.e: 5 + 3 = 8, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 5 and add 3 each time. 5 is where the pattern starts. It is not the jump.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 3,490 + 10 = 3,500. 349 tens + 1 ten = 350 tens, so the answer is 3,500.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 500 less. 7,000 − 500 = 6,500. The numbers get smaller, so keep subtracting 500.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 250 more. 1,750 + 250 = 2,000. Counting by 250s, the numbers end in 000, 250, 500 or 750.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 4,995 + 5 = 5,000. 4,996 adds only 1. 5,995 changes the thousands digit.

items.q: Start at 2,600. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on by 200s 4 times: 2,800, 3,000, 3,200, 3,400. 3,200 makes only 3 jumps.

items.q: Start at 5,000. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back by 250s 3 times: 4,750, 4,500, 4,250. 5,750 goes the wrong way.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 9,400 and subtract 1,000 each time
Start at 9,400 and subtract 100 each time
Start at 9,400 and subtract 10 each time
Start at 9,400 and add 100 each time
items.e: 9,400 − 100 = 9,300, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 9,400 and subtract 100 each time. The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
c: Start at 2,025 and add 2,025 each time
Start at 2,025 and subtract 25 each time
Start at 2,025 and add 25 each time
Start at 25 and add 25 each time
items.e: 2,025 + 25 = 2,050, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 2,025 and add 25 each time. 2,025 is the start, not the jump.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
4, 8, 16, 32, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 8, 16, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 2 times the one before: 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16, 16 × 2 = 32. The rule is Multiply by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
20, 45, 70, 95, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 45 − 20 = 25, 70 − 45 = 25, 95 − 70 = 25. Each number is 25 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 25.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
200, 185, 170, 155, …
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts. 200 − 185 = 15, 185 − 170 = 15, 170 − 155 = 15. Each number is 15 less than the one before: Subtract 15.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
23, 28, 33, 38, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 28 − 23 = 5, 33 − 28 = 5, 38 − 33 = 5. Each number is 5 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 5.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
2, 6, 18, 54, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 12, 36, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 3 times the one before: 2 × 3 = 6, 6 × 3 = 18, 18 × 3 = 54. The rule is Multiply by 3.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
28, 35, 42, 49, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 35 − 28 = 7, 42 − 35 = 7, 49 − 42 = 7. Each number is 7 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 7.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
3, 6, 12, 24, …
items.e: The jumps are 3, 6, 12, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 2 times the one before: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24. The rule is Multiply by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
1, 5, 25, 125, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 20, 100, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 5 times the one before: 1 × 5 = 5, 5 × 5 = 25, 25 × 5 = 125. The rule is Multiply by 5.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
28, 39, 50, 61, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 39 − 28 = 11, 50 − 39 = 11, 61 − 50 = 11. Each number is 11 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 11.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
1,000, 975, 950, 925, …
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts. 1,000 − 975 = 25, 975 − 950 = 25, 950 − 925 = 25. Each number is 25 less than the one before: Subtract 25.

items.q: How many counters are there? Is the number odd or even?
items.e: Make pairs: 6 pairs and 1 counter left over. One left over means odd.

items.q: How many counters are there? Is the number odd or even?
items.e: Make pairs: 8 pairs and none left over. Every counter has a partner, so 16 is even.

items.q: How many counters are there? Is the number odd or even?
items.e: Make pairs: 9 pairs and 1 counter left over. One left over means odd.

items.q: How many counters are there? Is the number odd or even?
items.e: Make pairs: 11 pairs and none left over. Every counter has a partner, so 22 is even.

items.q: Is 4,537 odd or even?
items.e: Only the ones digit matters. 4,537 ends in 7, and 7 is odd, so 4,537 is odd. The first digit, 4, does not tell you.

items.q: Is 3,718 odd or even?
items.e: Only the ones digit matters. 3,718 ends in 8, and 8 is even, so 3,718 is even. The first digit, 3, does not tell you.

items.q: Is 6,290 odd or even?
items.e: Only the ones digit matters. 6,290 ends in 0, and 0 is even, so 6,290 is even. The first digit, 6, does not tell you.

items.q: Is 8,005 odd or even?
items.e: Only the ones digit matters. 8,005 ends in 5, and 5 is odd, so 8,005 is odd. The first digit, 8, does not tell you.

items.q: Is 0 odd or even?
items.e: 0 is even. Counting by 2s starts at 0: 0, 2, 4, 6. With 0 objects nothing is left over, and 10, 20 and 300 are even because they end in 0.

items.q: Which number is even?
items.e: Look at the ones digits only: 6, 7, 1, 3. 3,576 ends in 6, so it is even. The first digit does not matter.

items.q: An odd number + an odd number. The answer is …
items.e: Each odd number has 1 left over. The two left-overs make a new pair, so nothing is left: always even. Example: 3 + 5 = 8.

items.q: An even number + an even number. The answer is …
items.e: Both numbers are all pairs, so the total is all pairs: always even. Example: 4 + 6 = 10.

items.q: An odd number + an even number. The answer is …
items.e: The even number is all pairs. The odd number still has 1 left over, so the total is always odd. Example: 7 + 4 = 11.

items.q: An odd number × an odd number. The answer is …
items.e: 3 × 5 is 3 groups of 5. Two of the groups make 10, which is even. One group of 5 is left, and even + odd = odd. So the answer is always odd: 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: An even number × an odd number. The answer is …
items.e: An even number of equal groups can be paired group with group, so the answer is always even. Example: 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: An even number × an even number. The answer is …
items.e: Groups of an even number are all pairs, so the answer is always even. Example: 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: An odd number − an odd number. The answer is …
items.e: Taking away an odd number takes away the 1 left over too, so only pairs are left: always even. Example: 9 − 3 = 6.

items.q: An even number − an odd number. The answer is …
items.e: Taking an odd number from all pairs breaks one pair and leaves 1 over: always odd. Example: 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: How many counters altogether? Is the total odd or even?
items.e: Red: 7 is odd. Green: 5 is odd. Odd + odd = even, so 7 + 5 = 12 is even. The two left-over counters make a new pair.

items.q: How many counters altogether? Is the total odd or even?
items.e: Red: 6 is even. Green: 9 is odd. Even + odd = odd, so 6 + 9 = 15 is odd.

items.q: The rule is “start at 5 and add 3 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 3 = 27. 5 + 27 = 32. 35 makes 10 jumps. 30 is 10 × 3, but the pattern starts at 5.

items.q: What number is missing?
What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is +25. Go back one step from 1,475: 1,475 − 25 = 1,450. 1,550 goes the wrong way.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 20?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 3 each time. From Figure 1 to Figure 20 there are 19 jumps: 19 × 3 = 57. 4 + 57 = 61. 80 is 20 × 4, but only Figure 1 has 4 sticks.

items.q: Rehan runs 1.5 km on day 1. He adds 0.5 km each day. How far does he run on day 6?
items.e: Add 0.5 km each day: 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0 km. 3.5 km is day 5. 3.0 km is 6 × 0.5, but the pattern starts at 1.5.

items.q: Tables are pushed together in a row. 1 table seats 4 people, 2 tables seat 6 and 3 tables seat 8. How many people can sit at 10 tables?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 2 for each table. From 1 table to 10 tables there are 9 jumps: 9 × 2 = 18. 4 + 18 = 22. 40 counts 4 people at every table.

items.q: A city bus leaves the stop every 15 minutes. The first bus leaves at 7:05 a.m. When does the 5th bus leave?
items.e: Add 15 minutes each time: 7:05, 7:20, 7:35, 7:50, 8:05 a.m. From the 1st bus to the 5th there are 4 jumps. 8:20 a.m. makes 5 jumps.

items.q: The gym floor has a row of 40 tiles in the pattern blue, blue, white, blue, blue, white … How many white tiles are in the row?
items.e: White tiles are at 3, 6, 9 … 39. 39 = 3 × 13, so there are 13 white tiles. Tile 40 is blue. 27 is the number of blue tiles. 14 counts one white tile too many.

items.q: The school library has 2,450 books. It gets 150 new books each month. After how many months will it have 3,200 books?
items.e: Count by 150s from 2,450: 2,600, 2,750, 2,900, 3,050, 3,200. That is 5 months. 750 is the number of new books, not the number of months.

items.q: An ice rink tank holds 5,000 L of water. It drains 250 L each minute. How much water is left after 8 minutes?
items.e: Subtract 250 L each minute. 8 × 250 = 2,000. 5,000 − 2,000 = 3,000 L. 7,000 goes the wrong way. 4,750 subtracts only once.

items.q:
The rule is Add 8. What number comes next?
22, 30, 38, 46, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 46 + 8 = 54.

items.q:
The rule is Multiply by 3. What number comes next?
2, 6, 18, 54, ?
items.e: Multiply the last number by 3: 54 × 3 = 162. (Adding the same jump does not work: the jumps get bigger each time.)

items.q:
The rule is Subtract 50. What number comes next?
1,000, 950, 900, 850, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 850 − 50 = 800.

items.q:
The rule is Add 250. What number comes next?
1,250, 1,500, 1,750, 2,000, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 2,000 + 250 = 2,250.

items.q:
The rule is Multiply by 4. What number comes next?
1, 4, 16, 64, ?
items.e: Multiply the last number by 4: 64 × 4 = 256. (Adding the same jump does not work: the jumps get bigger each time.)

items.q:
The rule is Multiply by 2. What number comes next?
5, 10, 20, 40, 80, ?
items.e: Multiply the last number by 2: 80 × 2 = 160. (Adding the same jump does not work: the jumps get bigger each time.)

items.q:
The rule is Multiply by 2. What number comes next?
3, 6, 12, 24, ?
items.e: Multiply the last number by 2: 24 × 2 = 48. (Adding the same jump does not work: the jumps get bigger each time.)

items.q:
The rule is Add 15. What number comes next?
65, 80, 95, 110, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 110 + 15 = 125.

items.q:
The rule is Subtract 7. What number comes next?
102, 95, 88, 81, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 81 − 7 = 74.

items.q:
The rule is Add 7. What number comes next?
13, 20, 27, 34, ?
items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 34 + 7 = 41.
